newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares rebound to end higher.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares rebound to end higher.

text.p: Swedish shares ended higher on Friday in a rebound after having been depressed the other days of the week.
"It is a strong bourse, driven by flows," a trader said. "Many foreigners have returned to the market...Interest rates have come down somewhat and it seems as if we are over the worst hiccup."
The exchange's general index jumped 1.23 percent to 2,660.04 in turnover of 5.23 billion crowns.
The market was supported by telecoms group Ericsson which rebounded 6.5 crowns to 254.
Drugs major Astra rose 2.5 crowns to 347.5 and automotive group Volvo gained three to 190.

The bank sector was the strongest, surging 2.65 percent with S-E-Banken up two to 85, Handelsbanken gaining seven to 228 and Swedbank up 6.5 to 141.5. Nordbanken kept falling, however, down two to 255.

Insurance companies also belonged to the winners as they recovered from losses earlier in the week on lower bond yields. Trygg-Hansa leaped 8.5 crowns to 146.5 and Skandia closed 12 crowns higher at 227.
